name: Vādirāja
dates_notes: Usually placed in the eleventh century from the Akalaṅka commentarial tradition. This Digambara author must be distinguished from later Mādhva Vādirājas.
core_thesis: Vādirāja continues the Digambara logical tradition through an extended exposition of Akalaṅka's theory of valid cognition. His contribution is to clarify and transmit Jaina epistemology in a debate-facing scholastic idiom rather than to found a separate doctrinal school.

engaged_works.title: Nyaya-Viniscaya-Vivarana
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely transmitted as Vādirāja's commentary on Akalaṅka's *Nyāya-Viniścaya*.
engaged_works.summary: A detailed commentary on Akalaṅka's treatment of perception, inference, and testimony. It is an important source for the mature Digambara reading of Jaina pramāṇa theory and its disputes with Buddhist epistemology.
